meta.note: Base phase only. The formal 19-week marathon block starts 2026-12-07 and gets built from the week-16 test results.

foundation.notes: Real running background (sub-6 HS mile) but zero current run volume. Muscular build at 5'5"/190lb. Engine is well ahead of connective-tissue readiness — that gap is the whole risk.

strengths.evidence: sub-6 HS mile; 8:40/mi off zero training

limiters.evidence: no current run volume; tendon/bone adapts 12-24wk

targets.note: Locked in Feb/Mar 2027 off actual long-run and tempo data, per handoff.

weightPlan.protein: 170-190 g/day throughout — protects muscle through the deficit

phases.name: Base
physiologicalGoals: Mitochondrial density and capillarization (the 4-12 week adaptations)
Tendon and bone loading tolerance (the 12-24 week adaptation — the real constraint)

weeks.focus: Establish the habit. Run/walk only — no continuous running yet.

workouts.name: Strength — Foundation
workouts.humanReadable:
Bodyweight squat 3x12
Push-up 3x max (scale to incline)
Glute bridge 3x15
Plank 3x40s
Dead bug 3x10/side
Calf raise 3x20  — tibialis + calf work is your injury insurance
workouts.description: Lift before the week's running load accumulates.

workouts.name: Easy run
workouts.humanReadable:
Run/walk: 2 min run / 2 min walk, repeat for the full distance.
The walk breaks are not optional and not a failure — they are what lets your tendons catch up to your engine.
Effort: you should be able to speak full sentences the entire time.

workouts.name: Rest
workouts.humanReadable:
Full rest, or a 20-30 min walk if you're restless.
Adaptation happens today, not on the run days.

After a 10-min easy warm-up, run 1 mile as hard as you can sustain, then jog the rest easy.
This replaces the estimated zones with real ones. If anything hurts, skip it — there will be another chance.

workouts.name: Rest
workouts.humanReadable:
Full rest, or a 20-30 min walk if you're restless.
Adaptation happens today, not on the run days.

workouts.name: Easy run
workouts.humanReadable:
Continuous, conversational pace. If you can't talk in full sentences, you're going too fast — this is the single most common way beginners stall out.
Estimated pace ~10:30-12:00/mi, but run by feel, not by number.
Middle portion: 10-15 min at steady effort — comfortably hard, still controlled. Not a race.

workouts.name: Strength — Maintain + Power
workouts.humanReadable:
Squat 3x5 (heavier, low volume)
Pull-up 4x max
Push-up 4x max
Sit-up 3x2min  — full PST event, time it
Box step-up 3x8/side
Pogo hops 3x20  — tendon stiffness for running economy
workouts.description: Second lift. Keep it 24h clear of the long run.

workouts.name: Long run
workouts.humanReadable:
Continuous, conversational pace. If you can't talk in full sentences, you're going too fast — this is the single most common way beginners stall out.
Estimated pace ~10:30-12:00/mi, but run by feel, not by number.
Last mile: pick it up slightly if you feel good. Never more than that.

workouts.name: Recovery run
workouts.humanReadable:
Genuinely easy. Slower than your easy pace. This run exists to move blood through tired legs, not to build fitness.
If you feel worse at the end than the start, you ran it too hard.

BLOCK-TRANSITION TEST: after a 15-min warm-up, run a hard 2 miles at the fastest pace you could hold for an hour.
This sets the paces for the entire formal block. Do not skip it.
